key_insight: CostStart learns simplex warm-start decisions from measured computational cost because fewer pivots and greater overlap with an optimal basis do not reliably imply faster solves.
engineering_relevance: Cost-aware warm starts can accelerate LP solving by choosing both the starting basis and solver settings, while retaining the option to use the default start.
method: Use supervised learning to predict which variables belong in an optimal basis.
Train a small policy on measured CPU instruction counts.
Choose how many predicted columns to use, the simplex algorithm and pricing rule, or no warm start.
evidence_signal: Across 25 LP classes, CostStart roughly halves default-start solve time on unseen instances from training classes, including instances four times the training size, and is 1.4–2.2× faster than two retrained published methods.
watch_item: Generalization to new LP classes and transfer of instruction-count-based decisions across hardware or solver implementations remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
